answers.answer: A player rules a clearing by having more total warriors plus buildings there than each other player. Tokens and pawns do not count. An ordinary tie means nobody rules; the Eyrie wins a tie for most if it has at least one Eyrie piece there. The Vagabond cannot rule or prevent another player from ruling.
answers.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle: rule is determined by warriors plus buildings; tokens and pawns excluded; Eyrie tie exception and Vagabond exception stated.

answers.answer: Move any positive number of your warriors or pawns from one clearing along a linking path to an adjacent clearing. You must rule the origin, destination, or both, and recheck rule for each move. The same pieces may move repeatedly, including multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect says otherwise.
answers.evidence: Move (4.2): positive number, adjacent linking path, rule at either/both ends, repeated moves allowed; rivers are not paths.

answers.answer: The defender may play one matching ambush (birds are wild); the attacker may foil with a matching ambush. The defender's ambush is discarded either way; if unfoiled it deals two immediate hits, not capped by defending warriors, and battle ends immediately if no attacking warriors or pawns remain. Resolve before-roll effects, roll (higher die is attacker's hits, lower is defender's; ties equal), then after-roll effects. Rolled hits are capped by each side's own warriors, except Alliance defense reverses the dice and Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead of warriors. Add extra hits without a warrior cap and subtract ignored hits; if defender has no warriors, attacker gets one defenseless hit (for Vagabond, no undamaged swords means defenseless). Each hit removes one opposing piece. The side taking hits chooses removal order, but must remove all its warriors before its buildings/tokens; both sides deal their counted hits. A player who removes an enemy building or token scores one VP each, including a defender or removal outside battle.
answers.evidence: Battle (4.3), six steps: Ambush through Deal hits; removal priority and one VP per enemy building/token are specified.

answers.answer: Craft a hand card by activating crafting pieces that match the crafting icons at the card's bottom left, not by paying its card suit. Each crafting piece activates once per turn, except the Vagabond may reactivate its pawn by exhausting more hammers. Item cards require that item in the map supply or cannot be crafted. You cannot craft an identical persistent effect already in your play area.
answers.evidence: Craft (4.1): icons, once-per-turn activation and Vagabond exception; item supply prerequisite; duplicate persistent effect prohibition.

answers.answer: During your own Daylight, at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from hand into your play area; remove your score marker and stop scoring VP. You cannot remove or replace the activated card. At the start of your own Birdsong, mouse/rabbit/fox dominance wins if you rule three clearings of that suit; bird dominance wins if you rule two diagonally opposite corner clearings. Meeting a condition earlier does not win immediately.
answers.evidence: Dominance (3.3): timing, threshold, scoring marker, non-replacement, and suit victory conditions.

answers.answer: When a dominance card would enter the discard pile, put it near the map as available instead. During their own Daylight, a player may spend a matching-suit card to take an available dominance card into hand. Available bird dominance remains bird, so it must be paid for with a bird card; a bird card can pay for non-bird dominance.
answers.evidence: Dominance (3.3): discard destination and taking available cards; bird dominance stays bird and payment rules stated.

answers.answer: Standard setup uses faction setup order Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond; this is separate from turn order. With two players, remove all four dominance cards, shuffle the shared deck, and deal each player three cards. Put a ruin in each of the four R slots; the slots are occupied, but items are hidden under ruins only during Vagabond setup. With no Vagabond, ruins have no items. Stock the map supply with two boots, two bags, one crossbow, one hammer, two swords, two tea, and two coins. The faction-specific setup details beyond these points are not requested by the summary's setup description for two-player setup as a whole.
answers.evidence: Setup: steps 3–7 give two-player deck/hand, ruin and item supply setup, and faction setup order; each faction's setup is listed separately in the following subsections.

answers.answer: Only the Marquise may place pieces in the keep's clearing; other players may move pieces into it. If removed, the keep cannot be placed again. Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, the Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the keep clearing instead of supply; this can happen outside battle. Without a keep, there is no Field Hospitals destination.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat—Keep: placement rule and Field Hospitals; keep cannot be placed again once removed.

answers.answer: In Daylight, the Marquise first crafts with workshops, then takes up to three actions plus one action per bird card spent outside an action, in any order and number (subject to Recruit's once-per-turn limit). March is a compound action of up to two moves; either may use the same or different warriors, and you cannot interrupt it to spend a bird card or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter, only once per turn. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill's clearing to place one wood there.
answers.evidence: Marquise Daylight: craft first, action allowance and action descriptions for March, Recruit, and Overwork.

answers.answer: Choose a clearing the Marquise rules with an open building slot and choose the building type. Take the leftmost building of that type. Pay the column's wood cost using wood in the target clearing or in other ruled clearings connected to it by an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score the VP shown on the uncovered track space. Building requires the full cost, available building, and legal slot.
answers.evidence: Marquise Build: rule/open slot, leftmost building, linked ruled clearing wood network, and score on uncovered space.

answers.answer: Birdsong: (1) Emergency Orders—if the hand is empty, draw one card; (2) Add to Decree—add one or two hand cards, with at most one bird card, to any columns; (3) A New Roost—if there are no roosts on the map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can be placed.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties—Birdsong, in order: the three steps and no-roost placement requirement.

answers.answer: After crafting with roosts, resolve every Decree card by column in Recruit, Move, Battle, Build order; choose the card order freely within each column, and birds are wild. Recruit places a warrior at a roost in a clearing matching the card (two with Charismatic); Move requires moving at least one warrior from a matching clearing and normal move legality; Battle starts in a matching clearing containing Eyrie warriors and an enemy; Build places a roost in a matching clearing the Eyrie rules, with an open slot and no roost already there. If any required action cannot be completed fully, Turmoil begins immediately.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Daylight: columns are Recruit → Move → Battle → Build; each action's matching clearing and Build requirements are given.

answers.answer: In Turmoil, lose one VP per bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard every Decree card except Viziers; flip the current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement (if none are face up, flip all leaders face up first); retuck Viziers in the new leader's columns. End Daylight and proceed to Evening. Turmoil does not remove Eyrie warriors or buildings from the map. Evening scoring and drawing still occur, even after Turmoil.
answers.evidence: Turmoil, in order: loss, discards, leader change, Vizier placement, end of Daylight, and map pieces; Evening explicitly follows.

answers.answer: Outrage triggers when another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. That player adds one matching card from hand to Supporters (birds count); a group move costs one card per affected move, not per warrior. If there is no matching card, including birds, the player shows their hand to the Alliance, which draws one deck card into Supporters. Supporter capacity still applies: without a base, the Alliance holds at most five and incoming cards beyond capacity are discarded; with any base, capacity is unlimited.
answers.evidence: Alliance Outrage and Supporters: triggers, payment, no-card procedure, and capacity rules.

answers.answer: In Birdsong, the Alliance may Revolt any number of times first, then Spread Sympathy any number of times. Revolt chooses a sympathetic clearing without a base, matching a base still on the board, and spends two matching supporters. It removes all enemy pieces, places the matching base, places warriors equal to the number of sympathetic clearings matching that base's printed suit (including the revolt clearing), adds one officer, and scores normal VP for removed enemy buildings/tokens. Spread Sympathy chooses an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if no sympathy is on the map; it spends the matching supporter cost shown above the next token. Martial Law adds one matching supporter if one other player's warriors number at least three in that clearing. Then place one sympathy token and score its uncovered space. The summary does not specify a separate eligibility condition for which matching base space must be available beyond a matching base still on the board for Revolt.
answers.evidence: Alliance Birdsong: Revolt and Spread Sympathy subsections state order, eligibility, supporter costs, martial law, placement, and results.

answers.answer: Train by spending a hand card matching a clearing with an Alliance base to place one warrior from supply in the Officers box; Supporters cannot pay for Train. Organize is an Evening military operation: remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing to place sympathy there and score the uncovered VP. Organize uses no supporters and has no adjacency or Martial Law requirement, but legal token placement is still required. If a base is removed, discard all supporters matching its clearing, including birds, remove half the officers rounded up, and if no bases remain discard excess supporters down to five.
answers.evidence: Alliance Daylight gives Train; Evening gives Organize; Losing a base states supporter and officer consequences.

answers.answer: At Birdsong, refresh two exhausted items for each tea already face up on the Refresh track, then three more; tea refreshed during this step adds no refresh that step. Slip is optional and moves to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors; it ignores effects preventing movement out. Normal Daylight Move exhausts one boot plus one extra boot if the destination has any warriors of a Hostile faction, ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest can move only to an adjacent clearing. If in a forest at Evening, Rest returns damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up, then ready tea/coins/bags go to tracks if possible; this does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. The Vagabond always draws one card plus one per face-up coin on track, even after Rest.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Birdsong, Daylight Move, and Evening steps: Refresh, Slip, Move, Rest, and draw.

answers.answer: Explore exhausts a torch in a ruin's clearing; take one hidden item face up into Satchel or track and score one VP if an item was taken. Remove the ruin when its last item is taken. A Quest exhausts its two listed items, completes the matching face-up quest, and rewards either VP equal to matching completed quests including this one, or two cards; then draw a replacement quest. Repair exhausts a hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel while keeping its current face; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if space permits. The summary does not give the specific item pairs required by each quest.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Daylight: Explore, Quest, and Repair describe costs and effects; quest item pairs are not enumerated.

answers.answer: Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes it Hostile, except the special allied-warrior battle-loss case, which is decided at battle end if more allied warriors were removed than items damaged. During battle on the Vagabond's own turn, Infamy scores one extra VP per hostile piece removed, except the warrior that first made that faction Hostile; ordinary building/token points are added. There is no Infamy while defending on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot move a Hostile relationship marker out of Hostile. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior; only if that enemy has no warriors in the clearing may another piece of that faction be removed.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Relationships: Hostile, Infamy, Aid, and Strike provisions.

answers.answer: With four or more players, during the Vagabond's own Daylight at 10 or more VP, the Vagabond may activate dominance to form a coalition with another player not already in a coalition. The partner must have the lowest VP among players other than the Vagabond; choose among ties. Put the Vagabond's score marker on the partner's faction board and stop scoring. If the partner wins, the Vagabond also wins, including when the partner wins through dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent; coalition does not grant Allied relationship powers.
answers.evidence: Vagabond coalition (9.2.8): eligibility, timing, threshold, partner choice, scoring marker, victory, and Hostile reset.
